scenario: A medical journal only publishes clinical trials that ran for at least 12 months, as shorter trials are considered insufficiently powered for the journal's standards. A systematic reviewer uses the published literature's average trial duration to characterise the field's research culture.

data.description: Journal only publishes trials with duration > 12 months. Underlying trial duration distribution assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = 8 months.

question: Published trials average 20 months. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean trial duration Î¼ across ALL conducted trials (including those too short to be published), and (b) the fraction of all conducted trials that appear in this journal.
naive_answer: The typical clinical trial lasts about 20 months since that is the published average.
naive_trap: About 32% of trials are shorter than 12 months and never appear in this journal. The true mean across all conducted trials is about 15.9 months â€” 4 months shorter than the published literature suggests. A reviewer concluding that 'the field conducts 20-month trials as standard' would overestimate typical resource commitments.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(12-mu)/8; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+8*norm.pdf(a)/sf-20 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,14,16)
assert abs(mu-15.85)<0.25
assert abs(norm.sf((12-mu)/8)-0.6848)<0.01
